notes: Similarity = 100 / (1 + D), where D = sum(w_i d_i) / sum(w_i) over the comparable features only. It is a rough index, not a validated probability.

Numeric features are compared on the same ~3.7 km baseline. Earth 90 m DEMs are averaged to the MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd cell size before slope and roughness are calculated. This way, the terrain values for both planets describe the same physical scale.
Landing suitability and environmental similarity are separate calculations. Neither one affects the other.

features.label: Regional slope (median, ~3.7 km baseline)
features.rationale: Terrain gradient on the same baseline on both planets. A scale of 1.5 deg means that a 1.5 deg difference gives d = 1.

features.label: Detrended relief (~3.7 km cells)
features.rationale: Standard deviation of elevation across the footprint, after a plane is removed, on matched cells. The scale is 100 m.

features.label: Terrain morphology
features.rationale: Landform labels (for example impact_crater, lava_plain, playa or alluvial_fan). Distance = 1 - |A and B| / |A or B|. The labels come from the literature and are listed for each site.

features.label: Mineralogy / composition
features.rationale: Mineral labels from the cited literature (for example basalt, clays, sulfates or carbonates). This uses the same Jaccard distance.

features.label: Aridity (mean precipitation)
features.rationale: Mars has no liquid precipitation, so its value is 0. Earth values come from NASA POWER climate data. Lower precipitation on Earth means a better dryness analog. The scale is 1 mm/day.

features.label: Top-of-atmosphere insolation (annual mean)
features.rationale: This is calculated the same way for both planets. However, it depends mostly on distance from the Sun, not on the site. So it is shown for information only (default weight 0) and is not used for matching.

noncomparable_disclosures: Atmospheric pressure: Mars surface pressure is about 0.636 kPa (6.36 mb). Earth's is 101.4 kPa (1014 mb) (NASA Mars and Earth Fact Sheets). No Earth site is comparable.
Gravity: Mars surface gravity is 3.73 m/s2. Earth's is 9.82 m/s2 (NASA Mars and Earth Fact Sheets).
Radiation: Mars has no global magnetic field and a thin atmosphere. Its surface radiation dose is far higher than anywhere on Earth.
Temperature: mean surface temperatures on Mars are far below any Earth analog. Temperature comparisons are qualitative only.
Elevation datum: Mars elevations are relative to the MOLA areoid (GMM3). Earth elevations are relative to the EGM2008 geoid. So absolute elevations are shown, but they are never subtracted.
